sentence: This project runs research on childhood and adolescent cancer, focused on developing better treatments for children with cancer.
This project builds a national community of scientists who study the relationships between aging and cancer in older cancer survivors.
This project studies how dying cells are cleared by phagocytosis and degradation, using the nematode as a model organism.
This project develops machine learning to classify non-cancer deaths in cancer patients with disabilities.
This project studies why pancreatic tumor cells respond to a combination treatment and tests other drugs that may strengthen its anticancer effects.
This project studies how brain development and genes contribute to externalizing disorders, using methods from genomics, neuroscience and informatics.
This project uses positron emission tomography imaging to see how brain stress response systems contribute to disorders such as posttraumatic stress disorder and dementia.
This project develops ways to engage donor family members and healthcare staff in research involving recently deceased humans, using qualitative data.
This project studies how a B cell protein called a ubiquitin ligase helps produce antibodies that protect against multiple Influenza A virus strains.
This project uses spatial statistics to study how distance and transportation affect access to opioid use disorder medications and mental health care.
This project teaches biostatistical methods, machine learning and data science for research on mental health disorders.
This project offers X-ray crystallography, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and cryo-electron microscopy to determine macromolecular structures for cancer researchers.
This project asks how neural circuitry for social behaviors in vertebrates is activated in brain cells, encoded in the genome and evolves among related species.
This project studies how pericytes contribute to capillary remodeling in pulmonary arterial hypertension, using mouse models and stem cell-derived cultures.
This project hosts a conference on machine learning in healthcare.
This project studies how short-term plasticity in brain connections affects behavioral flexibility, using behavioral experiments and modeling.
This project develops proteomics tools to understand the epigenetic mechanisms behind a set of neuroepigenetic syndromes.
This project tests fluorogenic imaging probes for complement convertase in antibody-mediated rejection.
This project uses population-based data to study how Medicare Advantage affects access to cancer treatment, quality and outcomes for older adults.
This project develops a vaccine to treat Alzheimer's disease and tests it in two transgenic mouse models and non-human primates.
